title: Web Security, OAuth & OpenID Connect
description: Production web security reference covering threat modeling, origins, TLS, cookies, sessions, XSS, CSRF, CSP, CORS, OAuth 2.0, PKCE, OpenID Connect, token validation, authorization, API protection, secrets, dependencies, logging, and incident response.

subtopics.title: Assets, Actors & Trust Boundaries
subtopics.description: Identify protected assets, attacker capabilities, entry points, data flows, dependencies, administrative paths, and abuse cases before selecting controls.

codeBlocks.code:
Assets: identities, money, personal data, secrets, availability
Actors: anonymous user, authenticated user, tenant admin, operator, dependency
Boundaries: browser↔edge, edge↔service, service↔database, tenant↔tenant
Abuse: enumeration, replay, privilege escalation, resource exhaustion, data exfiltration

callouts.title: Authentication Is Not Authorization
callouts.text: Knowing who a caller is does not prove they may perform an action on a specific resource. Enforce authorization server-side on every operation.

subtopics.title: Origins, TLS & Response Headers
subtopics.description: The origin tuple is scheme, host, and port. TLS protects transport; security headers constrain browser capabilities and framing.

codeBlocks.code:
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=()

callouts.title: Deploy HSTS Carefully
callouts.text: Confirm HTTPS works for all included subdomains before long max-age or preload. HSTS cannot repair certificate or mixed-content failures.

subtopics.title: XSS, Output Encoding & CSP
subtopics.description: Encode untrusted data for its exact HTML, attribute, URL, CSS, or JavaScript context. Prefer safe DOM APIs and use CSP as defense in depth.

callouts.title: Sanitization Is Context-Specific
callouts.text: If rich HTML is required, use a maintained allowlist sanitizer and keep it patched. Sanitized HTML is not automatically safe inside script, CSS, URL, or unsafe attribute contexts.

subtopics.title: Cookies & Server Sessions
subtopics.description: Use opaque, high-entropy session identifiers; rotate after authentication or privilege change; expire and revoke server-side; and protect cookies with appropriate attributes.

callouts.title: Do Not Store Authorization State Only in the Cookie
callouts.text: Roles and entitlements change. Resolve current authorization from trusted server state or use short-lived, validated claims with an explicit revocation strategy.

subtopics.title: CSRF, SameSite & CORS
subtopics.description: CSRF abuses ambient credentials; defend with SameSite, origin checks, anti-CSRF tokens, and safe-method discipline. CORS controls browser response access, not server authentication.

codeBlocks.code:
Origin: https://app.example.com
X-CSRF-Token: <session-bound-token>

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin

callouts.title: Simple Requests Can Still Mutate
callouts.text: Do not rely on preflight as CSRF protection. Reject state changes through GET and validate origin/token for credentialed mutations.

subtopics.title: Passwords, MFA & Account Recovery
subtopics.description: Hash passwords with a dedicated adaptive password hash, rate-limit authentication, support phishing-resistant MFA, and make recovery at least as secure as sign-in.

codeBlocks.code:
Password: Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt with reviewed parameters + unique salt
MFA: prefer passkeys/WebAuthn; protect enrollment and removal
Recovery: single-use short expiry, verified channel, session revocation
Detection: velocity/risk signals without leaking account existence

callouts.title: Never Log Authentication Secrets
callouts.text: Passwords, recovery codes, session IDs, authorization codes, access/refresh tokens, and MFA assertions must be redacted from logs, traces, analytics, and error reports.

subtopics.title: Roles, Authorization Code & PKCE
subtopics.description: OAuth delegates API access. OpenID Connect adds identity. Use Authorization Code with PKCE for browser/mobile clients and avoid implicit or resource-owner-password flows.

diagram.content:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User agent
  participant C as Client
  participant A as Authorization server
  participant R as Resource server
  C->>A: authorize + code_challenge + state
  A->>U: authenticate and consent
  A-->>C: authorization code
  C->>A: code + code_verifier
  A-->>C: tokens
  C->>R: access token
  R-->>C: protected resource

callouts.title: PKCE Does Not Replace redirect_uri Validation
callouts.text: Require exact registered redirect URIs, bind state to the browser transaction, use nonce for OIDC replay protection, and consume authorization codes once.

subtopics.title: Access, Refresh & ID Token Validation
subtopics.description: Access tokens authorize APIs; ID tokens communicate an authentication result to the client. Validate the right token for the right recipient and purpose.

codeBlocks.code:
Validate: signature/algorithm, issuer, audience, expiry/not-before
OIDC client: nonce and authorized-party rules where applicable
API: scopes/authorization plus resource ownership
Keys: trusted metadata, cache with bounded refresh, handle rotation

callouts.title: A Decoded JWT Is Not a Validated Token
callouts.text: Reject unexpected algorithms and issuers, validate audience and time claims, and never accept an ID token as an API access token merely because it is signed.

subtopics.title: Refresh Tokens, Client Types & Logout
subtopics.description: Public clients cannot keep a client secret. Rotate or sender-constrain refresh tokens where appropriate, detect reuse, and define local session, provider session, revocation, and logout separately.

codeBlocks.code:
Confidential web app: server-side token storage and client authentication
Browser/mobile public client: PKCE; no embedded secret
Refresh: rotate, bind family, revoke on reuse, expire by policy
Logout: clear local session + consider revocation/provider logout

callouts.title: Keep Tokens Out of URLs
callouts.text: URLs leak through history, referrers, logs, screenshots, and analytics. Authorization responses and token storage require deliberate browser and backend-for-frontend design.

subtopics.title: Validation, Authorization & Abuse Controls
subtopics.description: Validate syntax and domain constraints, parameterize interpreters, enforce object/function authorization, limit payload and work, and design idempotency for retries.

codeBlocks.code:
Request boundary: size/type/schema/depth limits
Authorization: action + object + tenant + current policy
Execution: parameterized SQL/commands/templates; SSRF allowlists
Abuse: per-identity and global quotas, concurrency, timeouts, pagination
Response: minimum fields, stable errors, no secret echo

callouts.title: Avoid User-Controlled Resource Selectors
callouts.text: File paths, URLs, class names, redirect targets, templates, and query fragments need allowlists or structured APIs—not string sanitization alone.

subtopics.title: Dependencies, Secrets & Security Logging
subtopics.description: Pin and review dependencies, generate provenance where available, rotate secrets, separate environments, and log security decisions without logging credentials or sensitive payloads.

codeBlocks.code:
Log: actor ID, action, target class/ID, decision, reason code, request/trace ID
Do not log: passwords, cookies, tokens, authorization headers, private keys
Alert: credential stuffing, token reuse, privilege changes, unusual exports
Retain: access-controlled, tamper-resistant, policy-aligned

callouts.title: Rotation Must Be Tested
callouts.text: A secret is not operationally rotatable until producers and consumers can overlap versions, reload safely, revoke the old value, and verify completion.

subtopics.title: Testing & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Combine design review, automated tests, dependency analysis, configuration scanning, dynamic testing, abuse testing, monitoring, and incident exercises.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Threat-model boundaries, enforce HTTPS, secure sessions, prevent XSS/CSRF, restrict CORS/CSP, use Authorization Code + PKCE, validate tokens, authorize every object/action, bound work, redact telemetry, patch dependencies, protect secrets, and rehearse revocation and incident response.
